districts.name: Bisbee
districts.verbatim_quote: The Bisbee (or Warren) district is in the south- eastern Mule Mountains, in the southern part of the county, immediately north of the Mexican border.

districts.name: Dos Cabezas
districts.verbatim_quote: The Dos Cabezas district is 18 miles southeast of Wilcox in the Dos Cabezas Mountains.

districts.name: Tombstone
districts.verbatim_quote: The Tombstone district, about 20 miles northwest of Bisbee in the Tombstone Hills, includes a group of low scattered mountains that extend northwest- ward from the Mule Mountains.

districts.name: Turquoise
districts.verbatim_quote: The Turquoise (Courtland, Gleeson) mining dis- trict lies on the east side of the Dragoon Mountains, about 14 miles due east of Tombstone and about 18 miles north-northeast of Bisbee.

districts.name: Banner
districts.verbatim_quote: The Banner (Christmas) district lies in the ex- treme southern tip of Gila County at the southeast end of the Dripping Springs Mountains.

districts.name: Globe-Miami
districts.verbatim_quote: The Globe-Miami district, in the foothills of the Pinal and Apache Mountains in the southwestern part of Gila County, is noted primarily for its cop- per deposits which have yielded considerable amounts of gold, silver, and lead.

districts.name: Ash Peak
districts.verbatim_quote: The Ash Peak district is 12 miles west of Duncan.

districts.name: Clifton-Morenci
districts.verbatim_quote: The Clifton-Morenci district is in west-central Greenlee County near the towns of Clifton and Morenci.

districts.name: Cave Creek
districts.verbatim_quote: The Cave Creek district, 25 to 45 miles north of Phoenix, was active at least as early as the 1890's, when the Phoenix and Maricopa mines were the major properties and were yielding gold ore. A few copper deposits were also worked before 1900 (Wilson and others, 1934, p. 164-165).

districts.name: Vulture
districts.verbatim_quote: The Vulture district is on the south side of the Vulture Mountains, in northwestern Maricopa County.

districts.name: Gold Basin
districts.verbatim_quote: The Gold Basin (Salt Springs) district is in the eastern part of the White Hills west of Hualpai Wash, 40 miles north of Hackberry and 60 miles north of Kingman.

districts.name: San Francisco
districts.verbatim_quote: The San Francisco district is near the south end of the Black Mountains about 29 miles by . road southwest of Kingman.

districts.name: Wallapai
districts.verbatim_quote: Located near the center of the Cerbat Mountains, which extend north-northwestward from Kingman for about 30 miles, the Wallapai district includes the mining camps of Chloride, Mineral Park, Cerbat, and Stockton.

districts.name: Weaver
districts.verbatim_quote: The Weaver district is in the northern Black Mountains, 10 to 25 miles west and northwest of Chloride.

districts.name: Ajo
districts.verbatim_quote: The Ajo district is in western Pima County, 125 miles west of Tucson.

districts.name: Greaterville
districts.verbatim_quote: The Greaterville district is in southeastern Pima County, about 34 airline miles southeast of Tucson.

districts.name: Mammoth
districts.verbatim_quote: The Mammoth (or Old Hat) district is in south- eastern Pinal County on the east flank of the Black Hills, about 50 miles northeast of Tucson.

districts.name: Ray
districts.verbatim_quote: The Ray (or Mineral Creek) district is in north- eastern Pinal County about 17 miles south of Miami.

districts.name: Superior
districts.verbatim_quote: The Superior (Pioneer) district is about 15 miles southwest of Miami and 12 miles northwest of Ray.

districts.name: Oro Blanco
districts.verbatim_quote: The Oro Blanco district is in western Santa Cruz County near Ruby, about 32 miles by road north- west of Nogales and about 70 miles by road south- southwest of Tucson.

districts.name: Agua Fria
districts.verbatim_quote: The Agua Fria district is southeast of Prescott along the headwaters of the Agua Fria River about 4% miles northeast of Mayer.

districts.name: Big Bug
districts.verbatim_quote: The Big Bug district, on the northeast slope of the Bradshaw Mountains, is about 12 miles east- southeast of Prescott.

districts.name: Black Canyon
districts.verbatim_quote: The Black Canyon district is in southeastern Yavapai County between the eastern foothills of the Bradshaw Mountains and the Agua Fria River, at Buinblebee.

districts.name: Black Rock
districts.verbatim_quote: The Black Rock district, about 12 to 15 miles northeast of Wickenburg, was prospected for cop- per and silver in the 1870's, but according to meager records the deposits were not developed until 1900 or later (Wilson and others, 1934, p. 62-65).

districts.name: Eureka
districts.verbatim_quote: The Eureka (Bagdad) district is in western Yavapai County, 42 miles west of Prescott.

districts.name: Hassayampa-Groom Creek
districts.verbatim_quote: The Hassayampa-Groom Creek district is on the western slopes of the Bradshaw Mountains, 6 miles south of Prescott.

districts.name: Jerome
districts.verbatim_quote: The Jerome (Verde) district is on the eastern slope of the Black Hills in northeast Yavapai County just west of the Verde River.

districts.name: Lynx Creek-Walker
districts.verbatim_quote: The Lynx Creek-Walker district is about 7 miles . southeast of Prescott.

districts.name: Martinez
districts.verbatim_quote: The Martinez district is in southwestern Yavapai County in the southeastern Date Creek Mountains a few miles northwest of Congress.

districts.name: Peck
districts.verbatim_quote: The Peck district is in the drainage area of Peck Canyon and Bear Creek, about 20 miles south- southeast of Prescott.

districts.name: Pine Grove-Tiger
districts.verbatim_quote: The Pine Grove-Tiger (Crown King) district is in the heart of the Bradshaw Mountains 40 miles by road southeast of Prescott; the Tiger camp lies immediately south of the Pine Grove camp.

districts.name: Tiptop
districts.verbatim_quote: The Tiptop district is in the southern foothills of the Bradshaw Mountains in southeastern Yavapai County, about 45 miles north-northwest of Phoenix.

districts.name: Weaver-Rich Hill
districts.verbatim_quote: The Weaver-Rich Hill district is in southwestern Yavapai County along the southwestern front of the Weaver Mountains, 5 to 8 miles east of Congress.

districts.name: Castle Dome
districts.verbatim_quote: The Castle Dome district is in south-central Yuma County in the southern Castle Dome Mountains, about 20 to 25 miles north of Well ton.

districts.name: Cienega
districts.verbatim_quote: The Cienega district is in northwestern Yuma County, 5 to 8 miles northeast of Parker.

districts.name: Dome
districts.verbatim_quote: The Dome (Gila City) district is at the north end of the Gila Mountains, about 15 miles east of Yuma.

districts.name: Ellsworth
districts.verbatim_quote: The Ellsworth (Harquahala) district is in the Little Harquahala Mountains, 5 to 10 miles south of Salome.

districts.name: Fortuna
districts.verbatim_quote: The Fortuna district is on the west flank of the central part of the Gila Mountains, 21 miles south- east of Yuma.

districts.name: Kofa
districts.verbatim_quote: The Kofa district is in the central part of the county, on the southwestern flank of the Kofa Mountains. · Nearly the entire gold output of this district came from the King of Arizona andthe North Star lode mines, discovered in 1896 and 1906 respectively.

districts.name: Laguna
districts.verbatim_quote: The Laguna district is immediately north of the Gila River and east of the Colorado River, at the south end of the Laguna Mountains.

districts.name: La Paz
districts.verbatim_quote: The La Paz (Weaver) district, in west-central Yuma County, is 9 miles west of Quartzite and 6 miles east of the Colorado River, along the west side of the Dome Mountains.

districts.name: Plomosa
districts.verbatim_quote: The Plomosa district is near the town of Quartzite on La Posa Plain, between the Plomosa Mountains on the east and the Dome Rock Mountains on the west.

source.citation: Koschmann, A. H., and Bergendahl, M. H., 1968, Principal Gold-Producing Districts of the United States: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 610, 283 p.
source.title: Principal Gold-Producing Districts of the United States
